pride_data.title: Structural architecture and function of the human NALCN channelosome
pride_data.projectDescription: Chemical cross-linking coupled to mass spectrometry was used to study the subunit organization of the NALCN channelosome consisting of the proteins NALCN, FAM155A, UNC79 and UNC80. Cross-linking data was generated using the reagents disuccinimidyl suberate (DSS), pimelic dihydrazide (PDH), and 4-(4,6-Dimethoxy-1,3,5-triazin-2-yl)-4-methylmorpholinium (DMTMM) chloride, and was analyzed in combination with data from cryo-electron microscopy.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Cross-linking was performed according to previously described procedures (Leitner et al., Nat. Protoc., 2014; Mohammadi et al., Anal. Chem., 2021). Cross-linked proteins were digested in solution using endoproteinase Lys-C and trypsin and fractionated by size-exclusion chromatography. LC-MS/MS analysis was performed on a Thermo Orbitrap Fusion Lumos mass spectrometer.  Further information can be found in the accompanying publication.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: MS/MS spectra were searched using xQuest/xProphet (Walzthoeni et al., Nat. Methods, 2012), version 2.1.5, against the sequences of the target proteins and identified contaminants (some of which were found to be interacting specifically with the core complex). The false discovery rate was controlled by searching against reversed sequences. Important xQuest search settings were as follows: Enzyme = trypsin, maximum number of missed cleavages = 2, MS mass tolerance = 15 ppm, MS/MS mass tolerance = 20 ppm. Reactive sites for the cross-linking reagents were defined as follows: K and protein N terminus for DSS, D and E for PDH, K with D and K with E for DMTMM. The false discovery rate was adjusted to <5% at the level of non-redundant cross-link peptide pairs.  Further information can be found in the accompanying publication.
keywords: Chemical cross-linking; dss; pdh; dmtmm; ion channel; sodium leak channel; nalcn
